$description: ViaVitae corner-radius tokens. The system is deliberately close to square. A church-vertical identity built on stone, print, inscription and liturgical book is undermined by the soft pill corners of a consumer app; the radius scale therefore tops out at 8px for anything structural and reserves large radii for two specific cases — an avatar and a pill button — where a round form is the meaning rather than a decoration.

meta.$description: Non-DTCG bookkeeping, ignored by DTCG-conformant tooling.
meta.name: radius

radius.$description: The scale. Each step is roughly double the previous, which keeps the relationship between a card's outer corner and the corner of an image inside it consistent: an inner element's radius should be the outer radius minus the padding between them, and a doubling scale makes that arithmetic land on a token rather than between two.

none.$description: Square. The default for a page section, a full-bleed image, a table and anything that meets a viewport edge. Most of the system is none.

xs.$description: Badge, tag, inline chip, keyboard key hint, the corner of a table cell fill.

sm.$description: THE DEFAULT for a control: button, input, select, checkbox, textarea. Small enough to read as precise, large enough to avoid the harsh 1px corner that looks like a rendering defect on a low-density display.

lg.$description: Card, dialog, image inside a card, modal. The largest structural radius in the system.

xl.$description: A feature panel or an oversized hero card on a marketing page, where the element is large enough that 8px reads as square. Not used inside a product UI.

pill.$description: Fully rounded. Two uses only: an avatar and a pill button or filter chip. Using 9999px rather than 50% because a percentage radius on a non-square element produces an ellipse, and a 44px-tall pill button with border-radius: 50% becomes an oval. 9999px clamps to half the shorter side and stays a pill at any size.

circle.$description: For a guaranteed-square element: an icon button with equal width and height, a status dot, a numbered step marker. 50% is correct here and wrong everywhere else.

com.viavitae.nesting.$description: Inner radius rule. When an element sits inside a rounded container with padding between them, the inner radius must be the outer radius minus the padding, floored at zero. A card at radius.lg (8px) with spacing.4 (16px) of padding contains an image at 8 - 16 = negative, so radius.none (0px) — the image is square and the card's corner does the rounding. Getting this wrong is the single most common visual defect in a hand-built design system: every inner element at the same radius as its container produces a visible gap of background at each corner, which reads as sloppiness even to someone who cannot name it.

com.viavitae.rejected.$description: Radii considered and declined, so the question is not reopened by the next designer.

entries.reason: Reads as a consumer mobile app. The identity is institutional and printed; 16px corners on a parish donation card make it look like a food-delivery tile.
A distinctive device, but it cannot be applied consistently across a card, a button and an image, so it appears once and then looks like a mistake everywhere else.

Requires either a mask-image with an SVG or a border-image, neither of which composes with a focus ring or a box-shadow correctly. The visual gain over 8px is small and the implementation cost lands on every consumer.
